identity.real_world_identity_notes: Lotus 98T, the Renault Gordini EF15B turbocharged car driven by Ayrton Senna and Johnny Dumfries in 1986. The program used both five- and six-speed Lotus/Hewland configurations; the generic record does not identify one chassis, driver, or race specification.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift.

The standard gate was read from the cockpit by watching the lever and the driver's hand through a shift, because these cars have no gate plate. The same method read three dogleg gates in dataset 0.3.28 that registered sources then corroborated.

AMS2 selects the aero configuration from the circuit rather than from the driver, so the same car reports a different identity depending on the track. Both observed identities are carried here: the suffixed high-downforce name seen at Laguna Seca, and the unsuffixed base name seen at Daytona. The selection screen offers no low-downforce package for this class, so this car has two aero identities and both are recorded. Only the high-downforce configuration was driven; the controls are shared because downforce does not change the gearbox, and the low-downforce identity is recorded as an untested aero configuration.

The gearbox is a racing Hewland, engaged by dog rings rather than synchronisers, so the driver must match revs on a downshift for the gear to engage cleanly. The downshift blip is therefore required, not optional.

Dog-ring construction is inferred from Hewland's design approach rather than stated by a reviewed source. A source showing this gearbox was synchronised would change the gearbox type and make the downshift blip optional.

The 1986 program used both five- and six-speed gearboxes. Period and retrospective accounts describe different allocations across chassis, drivers, and events, so a generic 98T record cannot assign one authentic count. AMS2's five and AC's six remain exact simulator observations, not authenticity verdicts.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.lotus-renault-98t-high-downforce.20260814t154354295z-af25e11d by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: The guided drive directly selected all six forward gears in the official Kunos implementation.

Kunos's official car list and the lotus_98t content id establish the official AC implementation. The guided drive directly established six forward gears, H-pattern actuation, clutch-required move-off, required lift and manual rev matching, no automatic cut or blip, and a round wheel without display or shift lights. Running clutch acceptance remains medium confidence because AC's clutch channel was already active while stopped and may report the car's own clutch.

claims.basis: Registered sources, including a period May 1986 report, establish the exact 98T and its real five- and six-speed configuration variants; both exact simulator identities were observed live.
The real configurations and both guided drives agree on driver-operated H-pattern actuation; the sources do not support collapsing the two real gear-count variants into one generic count.

The 98T program used both five- and six-speed gearboxes. A period May 1986 report says gearbox breakages left six-speed units for Senna's two cars while Dumfries used an old-type five-speed; a retrospective exact-chassis account describes another allocation. The generic record lacks chassis, driver, and race scope, so its authentic gear count remains open while each simulator keeps its directly observed implementation count.

The registered source names a Lotus / Hewland six-speed manual but does not state how it engages. Dog-ring construction is inferred from Hewland's design approach rather than stated by a reviewed source, so this value is medium confidence: a source showing the gearbox was synchronised would change it, and would make the downshift blip optional.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
